base.note: v94.1 restored two DA1 navigation keys that v94 omitted. This round reaches the same result in its own source tree rather than copying the Codex candidate.

changes.scope: Three changes. No WPCS sweep, no phpcbf, no suppression pass, no refactor. Plugin version unchanged.
detail: includes/flosc-request.php - 'catalog' and 'da1_export' added to flosc_nav_param_keys(). They were omitted in v94, and because admin/da1.php copies the array into $flosc_da1_get, the DA1 screen could not select a catalog from a URL and its Export TSV button did nothing. Nothing failed loudly. Codex found it by reading the diff.

admin/flow.php - the file-scope wp_unslash( $_POST ) read is gone. Two guarded helpers replace it: flosc_flow_requested_file_action() refuses anything that is not a POST from a user with edit_others_posts and names an action only when both the submit button and its file field are present, which is the exact condition the three branches always used; flosc_flow_posted_file_name() reads one field and is called only after check_admin_referer(). The duplicate, import and delete branches keep their own nonce check, their manage_options check and their wp_die messages unchanged.
tests/check_nav_param_keys.php - new gate. Resolves aliases of $flosc_get, collects every literal key read through any of them, and requires each to be declared. Reports the reverse direction too.
changes.note_on_suppressions: Three phpcs:ignore lines were written into admin/flow.php while drafting this round and then removed before commit. They hid five WordPress.Security.NonceVerification.Missing findings in the two new helpers. Those findings are true: the detector must read $_POST to learn which submit button was pressed, because a nonce cannot be verified before knowing which action was submitted, and the reader is called after check_admin_referer() but the sniff cannot follow that across a call. Both facts are written into the file's docblock instead of being silenced. The WPCS error count is 1525 rather than 1520 as a result. Plugin Check classes NonceVerification as a warning.

measurements.method: PHPCS 3.13.6 with WPCS 3.4.0 and PHPCompatibilityWP, run against a copy of the tree placed OUTSIDE pre-release-candidates/. phpcs.xml.dist carries <exclude-pattern>*/pre-release-candidates/*</exclude-pattern>, so a scan started inside a candidate folder matches zero files and completes in about 90ms. Any WPCS figure measured in place is meaningless.
measurements.gates: 41 PHP and 2 JS, all pass (40 PHP before this round; check_nav_param_keys.php is the 41st)

not_verified: No WordPress runtime was available. The plugin was not activated, no admin screen was rendered, and the duplicate, import and delete actions in admin/flow.php were not exercised against a real request.
Official Plugin Check (wp plugin check flosc) was not run: it needs wp-cli and a booting WordPress.
The release gate tests/verify-standards.sh was not run for the same reason - it requires wp-cli and refuses to report a pass for a tool that did not run.
flagged_for_decision: admin/create-sample-data.php is excluded from the artifact by both .distignore and the hard deny list in build-dist-zip.sh. That rule is inherited and was not changed in this round. It is a WP-CLI eval-file seeder: nothing requires or includes it and its own header says 'Run via: wp eval-file'. The Codex v94.1 candidate removed the rule, which is why that file is inside its zip. The decision belongs to a functional review, not to a remediation round.

admin/settings.php:370 still reads wp_unslash( $_POST ) at file scope. It is not being converted to a declared list: $flosc_post is read with 251 distinct keys across the tree and ten of them are built at runtime, such as $flosc_post[ $state . '_pill_icon' ]. An allowlist would silently drop fields and break saves.
